statement: The columns of A are linearly independent when the only solution to Ax = 0 is x = 0; no other combination Ax of the columns gives the zero vector. Equivalently the nullspace of A contains only the zero vector.
quotes: DEFINITION The columns of A are linearly independent when the only solution to Ax = 0 is x = 0. No other combination Ax of the columns gives the zero vector.
The columns are independent when the nullspace $N ( A )$ contains only the zero vector.

statement: Elimination applied to the augmented matrix [A b] produces [R d]; then Ax = b has the same solutions as the simpler system Rx = d.
quotes: Elimination on [A b] leads to [R d]. Then Ax = b is equivalent to Rx = d.
When we apply the usual elimination steps to A, reaching R, we also apply them to b.

statement: The projection matrix onto the column space C(A) is P = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T; it satisfies p = Pb.
quotes: The projection matrix is $P = A ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A ) ^ { - 1 } A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$
The projection matrix $\overset { \cdot } { P } = \overset { \cdot } { A } ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A ) ^ { - 1 } A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ gives $p = P b$

statement: Every subspace must contain the zero vector; this follows directly from the scalar-multiplication rule by choosing c = 0.
quotes: First fact: Every subspace contains the zero vector.

statement: The column space of A consists of all linear combinations of the columns of A, i.e. all vectors Ax; it is a subspace of R^m.
quotes: The column space consists of all linear combinations of the columns.
It is a vector space made up of column vectors.
